preRunSkillProbe.observation: Both sources correctly judged a finished author task did not finish M1. The old-source proposed AGENTS body lacked an explicit durable required-item gate; the candidate proposed body included it. This is evidence of a setup artifact improvement, not an immediate model judgment improvement. The candidate probe preceded a wording-only clarification distinguishing roadmap scope changes from evidence/status updates; the S0-S6 evaluation used the final hashed package.

judgment.materialSafetyOrCompletionDifference: None observed. Both arms completed R1/R2, maintained role and acceptance boundaries, and handed off the current state accurately.
judgment.boundedOperationalDifference: JOENESS did not append a repeated S5 verification note; Bare did. Bare's final documentation diff had 295 insertions/10 deletions across six tracked files; JOENESS had 188 insertions/9 deletions across six tracked files plus the expected setup-state directory. These are observed writing/friction differences, not proof of general superiority.
judgment.uniqueSetupValue: JOENESS installed a short, durable managed AGENTS completion gate and reusable setup state in S0. Bare independently created effective work instructions. The immediate task outcomes were materially equivalent.
judgment.humanReadability: UNVERIFIED: no blinded user rating of the two S6 handoffs was obtained.

limitations: One fictional project and one run per arm/stage cannot establish statistical performance superiority or reliability across other repositories, models, restarts, or longer histories.
The setup package and Core were evaluated together; this is not a Core-only attribution test.
The agent-generated project states were not repaired between stages and remain in isolated temporary Git projects, not production projects.
The exact final responses were captured as local tool output and terminal last-message files; this bounded JSON preserves thread IDs, outcomes, hashes, and limitations but not complete rollout logs.
The first S0 Bare attempt was invalid because of command policy, preserved above, and rerun once with unchanged prompt.
